div.l: The wordes mote be cosyn to the dede
Also I pray ȝow forȝeue it me
Al haue I nought sette folk in her degre
Here in this tale as they shulde stonde
My wit is short ȝe may wel vnderstonde
Gret chere made oure host vs eủerychon
And to the soper sette he vs anon
He serued vs with vitayles at the beste
Strong was the wyn and wel to drinke vs leste
A semely man oure host was with alle
For to ben a marchal in a lordes halle
A large man he was with eyen stepe
A fayrer burgeys is ther non in chepe
Bold of his speche and wys ⁊and wel y taught
And of manhode him lakked right naught
¶ Eke ther to he was right a mery man
And after soper to pleyen he bigan
And spak of m̉erthe among other thinges
Whan that we hadde made oure reknynges
And saide thus now lordinges trewely
Ȝe ben to me welcome right hertely
For by my trouthe ȝif that I shal not lye
I sawgh nought this ȝere so mery a companye
At ones in this herberwe as is now
Fayn wolde I done ȝow m̉erthe wiste I how
And of a m̉erthe I am right now bithought
To done ȝow ese and it shal coste nought
¶ Ȝe gon to Caunt̉erbury god ȝow spede
The blisful martir quite ȝow ȝoure mede
And wel I woot as ȝe gon by the weye
Ȝe shapen ȝow to talken and to pleye
For trewely confort ne m̉erthe is noon
To ride by the weye dombe as eny stoon
And therfore wole I maken ȝow disport
As I seide arst and don ȝow som confort
And ȝif ȝow liketh alle by oon assent
For to stonden at my Iugement
And for to werken as I shal ȝow seye
¶ To morwe whan we riden by the weye
